meta.draftedBy: AI-drafted from the cited web sources; no clinician has reviewed or approved any item
meta.purpose: Language-neutral list of conjunctivitis symptoms, risk factors, triggers, self-care and contact-your-clinic rules, each tied to a published source, so the app's AI observations and guided questions can be checked against something verifiable (PLAN.md D1, D7).
meta.regionNote: All sources are UK/US public-health pages. Malaysian practice, emergency numbers and clinic thresholds may differ; the pilot clinic must confirm before anything is shown to a patient as guidance.
meta.dTwoRule: Nothing in this file names a type (viral / bacterial / allergic) or a severity as a conclusion. Rules only produce an advice-to-contact message, never a diagnosis or severity label (PLAN.md D1/Q9).

translations.note: Translation counts as an adaptation of NHS content under the NHS terms, and medical wording needs review in each language.

items.labelEn: Dry eyes

actionRulesCandidates.note: PROPOSED rules only, status needs-clinician-decision. They produce an advice-to-contact message, never a severity or diagnosis label (D1). The sources disagree on thresholds; both wordings are kept. Emergency routing for injuries/chemical exposure is separate and not covered by these four sources (see gaps).

claims.says: Pain in the eyes, sensitivity to light, changes in vision like wavy lines or flashing, or very red eyes: ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111; these can be signs of a more serious eye problem.

claims.where: When do I need to see a doctor
claims.says: More conditional: a lot of pain, a very red eye, or blurry vision / light sensitivity that does not get better after wiping away discharge.
Contact a provider if vision is affected, there is light sensitivity, or pain is severe or getting worse.

rules.disagreement: S1 lists any pain or light sensitivity as urgent; S2 and S3 use more conditional wording (a lot of / severe / worsening / not improving after wiping discharge). A clinician must decide which wording and threshold the app uses.
rules.ownerNote: The owner reports light sensitivity and pain on opening the eyes during episodes, so this rule would fire in every episode. The pilot clinic should say what the app should advise (e.g. 'contact your clinic today') so it neither stays silent nor cries wolf.

claims.says: See a GP if symptoms have not cleared up within 7 days.

claims.where: When do I need to see a doctor
claims.says: Symptoms that do not get better after a few days, or get worse.
Contact a provider if symptoms last longer than 3 or 4 days.

rules.disagreement: Thresholds differ: 7 days (S1), 'a few days' (S2), 3 or 4 days (S3). A clinician must choose one.

claims.says: Swollen or red eyelids/skin around the eyes, or a headache alongside other symptoms, are reasons to contact a provider.
A baby under 30 days with red, sticky eyes: urgent GP appointment or NHS 111.
Call a doctor now if a baby has unusual eye discharge or puffy red eyelids.

gapsAndOpenQuestions: RECURRENCE: none of the four sources discusses repeated episodes (the owner has had four in about 20 months, Jan 2025 to Sep 2026, roughly 6-7 months apart). No claim about causes or prevention of recurrence is made here; ask the clinic what they advise and whether further assessment is appropriate.

TYPE vs SYMPTOMS: S2 states it can be hard to work out the exact cause because the symptoms are usually the same. The app therefore does not infer viral/bacterial/allergic from symptoms. Where a source ties a feature to a cause (S1 sticky pus contagious; S1 allergic watery not contagious; S3 crusts 'most often' bacteria), it is recorded only as that source's statement.

EXISTING RED FLAGS: patient-app/src/utils/severityUtils.ts has five emergency flags (sudden vision loss, flashing lights/floaters, severe pain after injury, chemical exposure, sharp-object injury). None of the four sources covers chemical exposure, injury or sudden vision loss, so those flags are not sourced here. They need their own published guidance (and Malaysian emergency numbers) before they are shown as advice.

SOURCES WANTED BUT NOT USED: CDC conjunctivitis pages (blocked automated access), NICE CKS (blocked), StatPearls/NCBI Bookshelf (captcha), American Academy of Ophthalmology pages (site forbids copying into AI systems without permission). Clinician-level criteria (e.g. when to refer, differences between types) should come from a clinician or from guidance obtained by the owner/clinic.
MALAYSIA: no Malaysian source (e.g. Ministry of Health patient information) was used. Thresholds, wording and facility types should be checked against local practice.
PAIN / LIGHT SENSITIVITY WORDING: S1 treats these as urgent; S2/S3 are more conditional. Needs the clinic's decision (see rule.contact_urgently).
TRANSLATION: no Bahasa Malaysia text yet; medical wording needs review.
SCALES: the 0-10 scales, 'easily / with pain / not at all', and 'a little / a lot' amounts are app design for clarity, not taken from sources.
